_note: B級ご当地グルメ・街の揚げ物の系譜。品目ハブ（/en/eat/bkyu/）の横並び表と、各系譜ページがここから描く。出典は docs/research/monja-bkyu-fry-2026-10-11.md と各系譜ページの sources。記事にしたのはコロッケ（天ぷらの屋台史・みしまコロッケを含む）だけ。せんべい汁・甲府鳥もつ煮・トルコライスはメモに素材があるが記事を書いていないので planned で era は「—」。もんじゃは konamono の系譜。富士宮・横手やきそばは yakisoba、ソースカツ丼は donburi、串カツは tonkatsu にあるので行を作っていない
name: B-grade local food and town fried food
nameJa: B級ご当地グルメ・街の揚げ物

lineages.name: Korokke and town fried food
lineages.nameJa: コロッケ・街の揚げ物

origin.place: From the French croquette, via Meiji-era magazines
origin.era: A recipe printed in 1895; potato korokke after c. 1907; a hit song c. 1918

cells.what: A breaded, deep-fried croquette; early recipes used shrimp or meat, the cheap version potato
cells.roots: Butchers made a potato-based korokke from scraps and fat; the danshaku potato spread around 1907
cells.fame: The Korokke Song of about 1918 spread the name; third-favourite dish in a 1922 army survey
cells.know: Mishima korokke (2008) is defined only by using Mishima potatoes; fillings and shape are each shop’s choice

cells.what: A chicken-stock soy hotpot with vegetables and konjac noodles, with Nanbu senbei broken into it
cells.roots: Nanbu senbei, a flour-salt-water cracker, kept as food where cold summers hurt the rice crop; a soup cracker made after the war
cells.fame: The name took hold in Heisei when Hachinohe tourism groups promoted it; B-1 gold in 2012
cells.know: About 200 restaurants in Hachinohe serve it, by the farm ministry’s count

cells.what: The name means simmered chicken giblets; the recipe is not confirmed here
cells.roots: Said to have been created around 1950 at Okuto, a soba shop founded in 1913

cells.what: Pilaf (or dry curry), a cutlet and spaghetti Napolitan on one plate
cells.roots: One restaurant is said to have devised the original
cells.fame: Called a grown-up’s kids’ lunch; Nagasaki city presents it as a local speciality
cells.know: Shops vary it with korokke, carbonara and more; the name’s origin is unconfirmed
